snippets: Indian semiconductor startups like Netrasemi, Mindgrove, and Agnit are nearing commercial production, with some already running customer pilots and aiming for large-scale output by late 2027. Government incentives are accelerating this progress, but worsening global supply chain pressures, particularly from China, are creating significant production challenges and extending delivery timelines.

Indian semiconductor startups like Netrasemi, Mindgrove Technologies and Agnit Semiconductors are close to commercialisation, with them running customer pilots and gearing up for large-scale production, even as supply chain pressures threaten to slow the momentum.

Netrasemi has already moved its flagship chip into production, handing samples to three customers that are now running pilots. Commercial volumes are expected by mid-2027. PeakXV-backed Mindgrove, whose chips target biometrics, motor controllers and industrial electronics, is eyeing commercial rollout by the end of this year.

"Two years ago, there was no reason to buy (CCTV cameras) from an Indian OEM because so much was coming from Taiwan or China at far lower prices. But suddenly we are seeing Indian OEMs come to the forefront. The government has a big role to play in creating that same market for chips," said Netrasemi cofounder and chief executive Jyothis Indirabhai.

# Netrasemi

Ara Eve Leo Sal

1x

Netrasemi Private Limited is an Indian fabless semiconductor company founded in 2020 and headquartered in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, specializing in the design of power-efficient Edge AI System-on-Chips (SoCs) and chiplet-based architectures for real-time AI applications in compact devices such as IoT sensors and video analytics systems.[1][2] The company was established by Jyothis Indirabhai, Sreejith Varma, and Deepa Geetha, with a focus on developing in-house intellectual property for full-stack Edge AI chips that enable optimal computing for small, low-power devices.[3][2] Notable products include the NETRA A2000, a mid-range AI SoC designed for video analytics, and the NETRA R1000, a microcontroller optimized for smart IoT sensors, alongside advanced offerings like the NETRA A4000.[4][5][6] In July 2025, Netrasemi raised approximately $12 million (INR 107 crore) in a Series A funding round led by Zoho Corporation and Unicorn India Ventures, following an earlier pre-Series A investment of Rs 10 crore from Unicorn India Ventures in December 2024 to support chip fabrication and R&D.[5][2][7] This funding underscores the company's role in advancing India's semiconductor ecosystem, particularly in edge computing innovations for AI-driven IoT applications.[3][2]

## Company Overview

### Legal and Incorporation Details

Netrasemi Private Limited is the full legal name of the company, registered as a private limited entity in India.[8] It was incorporated on August 19, 2020, under the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013, as a non-government company focused on semiconductor design activities.[9] The Corporate Identification Number (CIN) assigned to it is U31900KL2020PTC063707, reflecting its classification under the manufacturing sector for electrical machinery and equipment, with a specific emphasis on semiconductor-related operations in Kerala.[10] The registered office and corporate headquarters of Netrasemi Private Limited are located at 2F, GEM Building, TC 4/2324, TrEST Research Park, Opposite College of Engineering Trivandrum (CET), Sreekariyam, Kulathoor Road, Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, India, PIN 695016.[11] This address serves as the official base for its legal and operational activities, situated within a technology park that supports innovation in electronics and semiconductors. As a private limited company, it remains unlisted on any stock exchange, maintaining its status as a closely held entity without public shareholding.[8] The incorporation of Netrasemi was motivated by India's growing emphasis on semiconductor self-reliance, particularly in response to global supply chain disruptions during the COVID-19 pandemic, which highlighted the need for domestic chip design capabilities.[12] The company's establishment aligned with government initiatives like the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) and support from the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), which provide incentives such as fiscal benefits and access to shared infrastructure to foster startups in the sector.[13] These policies aimed to build a semiconductor-based product economy, enabling entities like Netrasemi to develop edge AI technologies without relying heavily on foreign manufacturing.[14]

### Core Business and Scale Indicators

Netrasemi Private Limited operates as a fabless semiconductor company specializing in the design of intelligent System-on-Chips (SoCs) and chiplet-based architectures tailored for edge computing and real-time AI applications in compact devices.[15][16] This focus enables on-device processing for applications such as video analytics and IoT sensing, without reliance on cloud infrastructure.[17] The company is classified within the semiconductor design sector, specifically under the electronics and AI hardware industry, adopting a fabless model that outsources manufacturing to third-party foundries rather than owning fabrication facilities.[15][18] Its typical customers include original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) in the IoT, smart sensors, edge computing, healthcare, and automotive sectors, who integrate Netrasemi's chips into products like consumer appliances and intelligent systems.[19] As of estimates from August 2025, Netrasemi employs approximately 50 individuals, reflecting its scale as an early-stage startup.[10] The company is headquartered in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, India, with no additional design centers publicly reported, and it relies on external foundries for production.[15][18] In terms of financial scale, Netrasemi remains an early-stage venture with reported revenue of ₹1.66 crore(approximately $200,000) for FY 2024-25 ending March 31, 2025, operating post its $12 million Series A funding round in July 2025.[10][20][2]

## History and Evolution

### Founding Background and Early Vision

Netrasemi Private Limited was founded in 2020 in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, by semiconductor veterans Jyothis Indirabhai, Sreejith Varma, and Deepa Geetha.[21] The founding team, drawing on their extensive expertise in the field, was motivated by the pressing need for efficient edge AI chips amid global supply chain disruptions and India's near-total dependence on imported semiconductors, which stands at approximately 99.99% for most applications.[21] This initiative sought to contribute to building a robust domestic semiconductor ecosystem, leveraging government incentives like design-linked programs to foster innovation in chip design.[21] The company's original vision centered on creating power-efficient System-on-Chips (SoCs) tailored for embedding artificial intelligence in resource-constrained devices, enabling on-device intelligence for faster, energy-efficient real-time decision-making.[22] By focusing on domain-specific hardware acceleration for AI, Netrasemi aimed to address critical gaps in India's semiconductor landscape, particularly in enabling applications such as surveillance, robotics, autonomous drones, and industrial automation without relying on cloud infrastructure.[21] As articulated by co-founder and CEO Jyothis Indirabhai, the company aims to build a unique set of chips with domain-specific hardware acceleration for AI, optimized for cost, energy efficiency, and high performance.[21] Early challenges for Netrasemi included bootstrapping in the highly capital-intensive semiconductor sector, where development cycles are long and costs—such as for a single mask set—can run into crores of rupees.[21] The founders prioritized building a strong intellectual property (IP) portfolio and refining their technologies internally, spending years hiring talent and validating their business plan to avoid the pitfalls of premature investment and scaling, following an initial seed funding round in 2021.[21][23] This cautious approach, as Indirabhai noted, ensured the company was "locked" to a well-conceived idea before advancing to prototyping and commercialization.[21]

### Key Milestones and Strategic Changes

Netrasemi Private Limited achieved a significant early milestone in December 2024 by securing Rs 10 crore(approximately $1.2 million) in a pre-Series A funding round, which was earmarked for the fabrication of its two flagship machine learning system-on-chips (SoCs): the Netra A2000 for AI video analytics and the Netra R1000 microcontroller tailored for smart IoT sensors.[24][25] This funding supported the transition from research and development to production-ready prototypes, enabling the company to advance its focus on edge AI solutions for real-time applications in compact devices.[26] Building on this momentum, Netrasemi raised $12 million (Rs 107 crore) in a Series A funding round in July 2025, led by Zoho Corporation and Unicorn India Ventures, to further scale its design capabilities and accelerate commercialization of edge AI chips.[5][2] The investment was strategically aimed at enhancing the company's in-house intellectual property for full-stack edge AI processors, reflecting a pivot toward domain-specific SoCs driven by growing market demand for efficient, low-power computing in IoT and video analytics sectors.[6] By this point, the Netra A2000 and R1000 had entered commercial use, marking Netrasemi's entry into IoT markets with patented technologies optimized for intelligent edge devices.[27] Strategically, these milestones underscored Netrasemi's evolution from an IP-centric approach to full SoC productization, emphasizing organic growth without mergers or acquisitions to maintain control over its chiplet-based architectures for modular edge computing.[26] This shift was rationalized by the need to address real-time AI requirements in small devices, allowing the company to adapt quickly to industry trends in semiconductor design for edge applications.[6]

## Promoters, Ownership and Governance

### Promoters and Ownership Structure

Netrasemi Private Limited was founded in 2020 by Jyothis Indirabhai, Deepa Geetha, and Sreejith Varma, who serve as its key promoters with extensive backgrounds in the semiconductor and technology sectors.[28][29] Jyothis Indirabhai, the CEO and co-founder, brings over 27 years of experience in the semiconductor domain, including roles at Intel Corporation and Hitachi Engineering Japan, as well as leadership in successful startups.[30] Deepa Geetha, the COO and co-founder, is a system design engineer with expertise in AI/ML, embedded computing, and semiconductor domains.[31] Sreejith Varma, the CTO and co-founder, previously worked as a consultant at Tata Elxsi and holds a degree from the College of Engineering, Trivandrum.[32] Initially, ownership was fully held by the promoters, reflecting a founder-centric structure typical for early-stage startups in the semiconductor industry.[33] This structure began to evolve with a pre-Series A round in which Unicorn India Ventures invested Rs 10 crore to support the development of Edge AI for IoT products.[34] The ownership underwent significant dilution following the Series A funding round in July 2024, where the company raised Rs 107 crore (approximately $12.5 million) led by Zoho Corporation and Unicorn India Ventures, with participation from Maithan Alloys.[35][36] Post-Series A, the co-founders collectively retain over 50% of the ownership, ensuring continued promoter control and alignment with the company's long-term vision, while the institutional investors hold a substantial minority stake.[37][33] The dilution amounted to nearly 45% of the promoters' original stake, with the company also establishing an ESOP pool to incentivize employees.[33] No public disclosures indicate significant cross-holdings among promoters or other entities.[37]

### Board Composition and Management Team

Netrasemi Private Limited's board of directors consists of five members as of the latest available records from June 2024, including a mix of founding executives and independent directors appointed in recent years.[8] The board includes Jyothis Indirabhai Sivasankarapillia, who serves as a director since the company's incorporation on August 19, 2020.[8] Other directors include Deepa Geetha, appointed on the same date as a co-founder and executive; Anil Prahladan, appointed on July 5, 2023; Kizhakkebhagathu Ajith Joy, appointed on July 5, 2023; and Lekshmi Nair, serving as an additional director since September 28, 2023.[8][38] The management team is led by the founding trio and supported by senior executives with expertise in semiconductors and AI technologies. Jyothis Indirabhai, CEO and co-founder, brings over 15 years of experience, including a role as Chief Executive Officer at Westghats Technologies from 2014 to 2020 and as Design Manager and Micro-architect at Intel from 2005 to 2014.[39] Deepa Geetha, COO and co-founder, is a system design engineer specializing in AI/ML, embedded computing, and semiconductor domains, with a focus on developing frameworks for edge AI chipsets.[31] Sreejith Varma, CTO and co-founder, previously worked as a consultant at Tata Elxsi and holds a Bachelor of Science from the College of Engineering, Trivandrum.[32] Additional key executives include Hariprasad C, Chief Strategy Officer; Dr. Koshy P. Vaidyan, Chief Delivery Officer; Rahul A.B., Chief Financial Officer; and Sujeet Jayan, General Manager of Marketing, all contributing domain expertise to drive Netrasemi's focus on edge AI innovations.[22] As an early-stage private company, Netrasemi's governance emphasizes founder-led continuity, with the board and management team reflecting a blend of technical proficiency and strategic oversight.[29]

## Business Model and Operations

### Operating Model and Workflow

Netrasemi operates as a fabless semiconductor company, focusing on the design and development of System-on-Chips (SoCs) and chiplet-based architectures without owning fabrication facilities.[6] This model emphasizes in-house intellectual property (IP) creation for edge AI applications.[40] The company's focus includes edge AI SoC design, which integrates hardware accelerators for neural processing and computer vision, and chiplet architecture development, leveraging technologies like UCIe for modular, multi-die systems.[40][6] The end-to-end workflow begins with IP conceptualization, where Netrasemi develops domain-specific architectures optimized for vector processing and multi-kernel efficiency in real-time AI scenarios.[40] This is followed by design simulation using proprietary low-code/no-code tools like NETRA Edge Studio to port algorithms, optimize performance, and ensure energy efficiency.[6] Once designs are finalized, the process advances to foundry tape-out, after which chips undergo testing to validate functionality before distribution to device manufacturers.[40][6] Netrasemi's sourcing strategy relies on global foundries such as TSMC for fabrication, utilizing advanced process nodes like 12nm to produce its SoCs, while relying on in-house frameworks for design tools.[6] This approach allows the company to focus resources on innovation in edge computing without the capital intensity of manufacturing.[40]

### Sourcing, Inventory, and KPIs

Netrasemi operates as a fabless semiconductor company, conducting in-house design and development of AI-enabled system-on-chips (SoCs) and silicon intellectual properties (IPs) while outsourcing fabrication and assembly to external foundries and partners.[41] This model allows the company to focus its internal resources on research and development (R&D) and prototyping, leveraging third-party manufacturing expertise to scale production without owning physical fabrication facilities.[2] Key operational KPIs for Netrasemi are not publicly detailed beyond basic financial indicators, but the company's structure supports metrics focused on design efficiency and partnership delivery, with recent funding aimed at enhancing R&D and manufacturing capacity to improve overall operational scalability.[41] For instance, net cash flow from operations stood at -₹36.12 lakh in FY 2023-24, reflecting early-stage investment in growth amid a revenue of ₹1.7 crore.[41]

## Infrastructure, Technology and Processes

### Facilities and R&D Capabilities

Netrasemi Private Limited operates as a fabless semiconductor company, meaning it does not own or manage its own manufacturing plants and instead relies on strategic partnerships with external foundries for chip production.[42][43] This model allows the company to focus resources on design and innovation while outsourcing fabrication to specialized partners, aligning with its emphasis on cost-efficient development of edge AI solutions.[27] The company's primary R&D and design center is located in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, within a 3,800-square-foot facility at the TrEST Research Park, which provides world-class infrastructure and mentorship for semiconductor innovation.[6] This center serves as the hub for developing advanced edge AI algorithms and chiplet-based architectures, enabling real-time processing in compact devices.[17] Incubated at TrEST, modeled after leading research parks like IIT Madras, the facility supports Netrasemi's focus on domain-specific system-on-chips for intelligent edge computing.[27] Warehousing and logistics operations at Netrasemi remain minimal, given its fabless structure, with primary emphasis on intellectual property (IP) storage and management rather than physical inventory of fabricated components.[6] Following its Series A funding round in July 2025, the company has allocated capital expenditures toward infrastructure enhancements, including expansions in R&D capabilities to support broader IP development and operational scaling.[35] Looking ahead, Netrasemi plans to utilize proceeds from its $12 million Series A funding to accelerate R&D initiatives, ramp up production partnerships, and expand its footprint, potentially including new offices to enhance global market reach.[5] This expansion aims to strengthen the company's position in the edge AI sector by scaling design and innovation efforts.[44]

### Technology Stack and Quality Systems

Netrasemi employs a domain-specific architecture (DSA) optimized for edge AI applications, integrating hardware kernels such as neural processing accelerators, computer vision accelerators, image signal processors, and video codecs to achieve real-time performance and power efficiency in System-on-Chips (SoCs).[40] This architecture features energy-efficient vector processing with a graph-like streaming mechanism and configurable pipelining, supporting multiple data granularities and minimizing CPU involvement for parallel execution of AI models.[40] Additionally, the company incorporates Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express (UCIe) technology for multi-die extensions, enabling scalable compute capabilities up to 100 TOPS in neural chips and hybrid processors.[40] To support software development, Netrasemi provides a low-code, no-code software framework that facilitates porting algorithms and AI models while optimizing hardware acceleration with reduced errors and development time.[40] This is complemented by the NetraSDK, a versatile development kit supporting TensorFlow, PyTorch, and ONNX frameworks, including a graph builder tool and sample applications for edge AI deployment.[45] For electronic design automation (EDA), Netrasemi receives infrastructure support through the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)'s Design Linked Incentive (DLI) scheme and Chips to Startup (C2S) programme, providing remote access to advanced EDA tools for chip design activities over three years.[46][45] This government-backed access aids in the design processes, which involve close collaboration with original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) in telecom, industrial, and surveillance sectors to align specifications with customer needs, as well as partnerships with international firms for joint AI chip development.[45] Regarding quality systems, Netrasemi emphasizes validation processes to ensure chips meet production standards prior to customer showcasing, as demonstrated in plans for its NetraA2000 and NetraR1000 products.[45] The company adheres to compliance requirements under MeitY's DLI and C2S initiatives, which promote indigenous semiconductor design aligned with Indian policies for secure and efficient edge computing solutions.[47] No specific quality certifications such as ISO 9001 or IATF 16949 are publicly documented for the company at this stage.

## Products, Customers and Markets

### Product Portfolio and Differentiation

Netrasemi's product portfolio centers on intelligent System-on-Chips (SoCs) and chiplet-based architectures tailored for edge computing and real-time AI in compact devices. The company's flagship offering is the A2000 AI video analytics chip, designed for efficient processing of video streams with low power consumption, enabling applications in surveillance and smart cameras. Another key product is the R1000 microcontroller, optimized for smart IoT sensors, which supports real-time data processing and connectivity in resource-constrained environments.[4][1] What differentiates Netrasemi's offerings is its design-led approach, emphasizing in-house intellectual property (IP) for low-power edge AI acceleration. This includes custom neural processing units (NPUs) that deliver high performance per watt, allowing devices to run complex AI models without relying on cloud connectivity. Furthermore, the adoption of chiplet modularity enables customizable architectures, where components can be mixed and matched to meet specific OEM requirements, reducing development time and costs compared to monolithic SoCs.[40][1][48] To support rapid adoption, Netrasemi provides sampling capabilities through early access programs for original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), offering prototypes and development kits to facilitate integration and testing. This aligns with the company's fabless operating model, focusing on design innovation while outsourcing manufacturing.[49]

### Customer Profile and Market Reach

Netrasemi's addressable markets center on edge computing applications, with a primary focus on domestic India alongside global markets for end-uses in smart IoT sensors and video analytics.[17][6] The company's solutions target sectors such as smart surveillance for AI-driven object detection and facial analytics, robotics and drones for sensor fusion and navigation, and industrial AI for predictive maintenance and anomaly detection in Industry 4.0 settings.[17] The customer profile comprises B2B original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) and institutions specializing in edge computing, who integrate Netrasemi's intelligent SoCs and chiplet-based architectures into small devices for real-time AI processing.[17][6] These customers benefit from tailored solutions like the A2000 AI video analytics chip, enabling low-latency, on-device intelligence in diverse applications. Sales channels are primarily direct to OEMs via custom contracts, providing pricing power through bespoke agreements, while strategic partnerships with foundries support manufacturing and distribution.[50] This approach facilitates targeted engagement in niche markets. As a fabless semiconductor firm, Netrasemi holds a niche position in the Indian edge AI market, emphasizing innovation in specialized SoCs for emerging applications.[6]

## Industry and Competitive Landscape

### Industry Dynamics and Trends

The global semiconductor industry, valued at approximately $627 billion in sales for 2024, continues to exhibit robust growth driven by advancements in artificial intelligence and related technologies.[51] Within this landscape, the edge AI subset is expanding rapidly, with projections indicating a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of around 21.7% from 2026 to 2033, fueled by the need for efficient, low-latency processing in devices such as those developed for IoT sensors and video analytics.[52] In India, government initiatives like the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for semiconductors provide fiscal support of up to 50% of project costs to encourage domestic manufacturing and attract investments, aiming to bolster the sector's contribution to the national economy.[53] Key demand drivers in the industry include the proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices and the demand for real-time AI applications, which necessitate specialized chips for edge computing to enable faster data processing and reduced reliance on cloud infrastructure.[54] Structural trends such as supply chain localization are also prominent, as geopolitical tensions and trade restrictions prompt companies to regionalize production and reduce vulnerabilities in global dependencies, with semiconductors increasingly shifting toward politically aligned ecosystems.[55] These dynamics directly influence sectors like edge AI for small devices, where localization efforts help mitigate disruptions in component sourcing. On the supply side, foundry capacity constraints persist despite planned expansions, with global semiconductor manufacturing capacity expected to grow by 6% in 2024 and 7% in 2025, yet challenges in scaling for advanced nodes create bottlenecks amid surging demand.[56] In India, the regulatory environment is shaped by the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM), an initiative under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology that seeks to establish a vibrant domestic ecosystem for design, fabrication, and assembly through targeted incentives and partnerships.[53] The industry remains highly sensitive to commodity fluctuations, particularly due to AI-driven demand outpacing supply in critical materials, impacting production costs across the value chain.[57] Additionally, USD-INR exchange rate volatility affects Indian firms through increased costs for imported raw materials and equipment, given the sector's heavy reliance on global imports.[58] Fabless companies, positioned upstream in the value chain focused on design and intellectual property, benefit from high gross margins—often exceeding 50% for AI-oriented firms—due to lower capital expenditures on manufacturing, but they face significant dependency on external foundries for production, exposing them to capacity shortages and geopolitical risks.[59] This model underscores the industry's emphasis on innovation in areas like intelligent SoCs for edge applications, while highlighting the need for diversified partnerships to ensure supply stability.[60]

### Competitive Moat and Peer Comparison

The semiconductor industry exhibits a fragmented structure in chip design, where numerous fabless companies compete by focusing on innovation and intellectual property, while fabrication is more consolidated among a few major foundries like TSMC and GlobalFoundries that dominate global capacity.[61] This bifurcation allows specialized design firms to leverage external manufacturing without the capital-intensive burden of owning fabs.[62] Entry barriers in the sector are substantial, primarily due to the need for advanced intellectual property (IP) development and access to specialized talent in areas like AI and edge computing.[63] For Netrasemi, its competitive moat lies in its in-house IP for full-stack edge AI chips, enabling real-time AI processing in resource-constrained devices.[6] In peer benchmarking, Netrasemi positions itself against global giants like Qualcomm, which offers broader edge AI SoCs with integrated connectivity but at higher development costs and potentially superior margins due to scale.[64] Among Indian peers, such as Saankhya Labs, Netrasemi shares similarities in focusing on SoC design, with Netrasemi targeting edge AI and IoT applications and Saankhya Labs emphasizing wireless 5G communication, both operating under fabless models in emerging markets.[65] The fabless design focus of companies like Netrasemi typically yields gross margins of 55-70%, significantly higher than the 40-50% for integrated device manufacturers (IDMs) that handle both design and fabrication, due to lower capital expenditures and operational efficiencies.[61][62][66]

## Financial Performance and Balance Sheet Analysis

### Revenue Growth and Margin Profile

Netrasemi Private Limited, as a fabless semiconductor startup founded in 2020, operated in a pre-revenue phase during its initial years before generating modest operating revenue of approximately₹1.7 crore in the financial year ending March 31, 2024 (FY24).[33] This marked a significant year-over-year revenue growth of 86.86% compared to FY23, reflecting early traction in chip design services and partnerships amid the company's transition from development to commercialization.[38] However, the overall revenue scale remains small, consistent with its status as an emerging player in the edge AI and IoT semiconductor space, where product launches like the A2000 AI chip are still scaling.[67] The company's margin profile in FY24 highlights a design-heavy cost structure typical of fabless operations, with an operating margin of -2.27%, indicating operational losses despite revenue growth.[11] EBITDA decreased by 37.03% year-over-year, underscoring high upfront investments in R&D and prototyping that pressured profitability in this early stage.[11] In contrast, the net profit margin stood at 1.31%, supported by a net profit of ₹5.3 lakh, which suggests some efficiency in managing non-operating items or cost controls.[11][33] No detailed breakdown of segment-wise contributions or specific R&D spend as a percentage of costs is publicly available, but the revenue primarily stems from chip design and porting services for partners.[1] Operating leverage potential for Netrasemi lies in scaling IP licensing and SoC deployments, which could improve margins as production volumes increase post- Series A funding in July 2024.[68] The company's FY24 financials, including revenue in the INR 1-100 crore range, position it for accelerated growth, though current metrics reflect the challenges of a high- R&D intensive sector.[11]

### Cash Flow, Balance Sheet, and Return Metrics

Netrasemi Private Limited, as a fabless semiconductor startup, exhibits a lean operational model that influences its cash flow dynamics, with historical data indicating operational cash burn prior to major funding events. In FY 2023-24, the company reported a negative net cash flow from operations of -₹36.12 lakh (per TheKredible; Inc42 reports ₹0.0), reflecting investments in early-stage R&D and product development typical for a nascent entity founded in 2020.[69][70] This pre-funding cash burn underscores the capital-intensive nature of semiconductor design, though the fabless approach minimizes physical infrastructure costs. Following the $12 million Series A funding round in July 2024, led by Zoho Corporation and Unicorn India Ventures, the infusion significantly bolstered liquidity, enabling a shift toward positive free cash flow in subsequent periods by providing runway for scaling operations without immediate revenue pressures.[5] The working capital cycle for Netrasemi remains short, benefiting from its fabless model that outsources manufacturing and relies on intellectual property and design services, resulting in high asset turnover driven by intangible assets such as IP portfolios. In FY 2023-24, the company's current ratio stood at 12.9, indicating robust short-term liquidity and efficient management of receivables and payables in a low-inventory environment.[70] Capital expenditure intensity is low for a fabless model, aligning with the sector's emphasis on innovation over heavy physical investments.[70] On the balance sheet, Netrasemi maintains a conservative structure with low debt and a strong cash position post-funding. As of FY 2023-24, total assets were ₹11.2 crore, with total liabilities at just ₹38 lakh and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.0, reflecting reliance on equity financing rather than borrowing.[70] The pre-Series A funding of Rs 10 crore in December 2023 contributed to a 2834% year-over-year growth in total assets for FY 2023-24, primarily through increased reserves and surplus, while the approximately $12 million cash infusion from the Series A round further strengthened reserves, positioning the company with ample liquidity for growth initiatives. Return metrics such as ROCE and ROE are nascent given the early revenue stage—FY 2023-24 revenue was ₹1.7 crore.[70][24] Overall, these elements highlight Netrasemi's financial resilience, with the balance sheet supporting sustained R&D amid limited but growing revenue streams.[69]

## Strategy and Growth Outlook

### Core Strengths and Initiatives

Netrasemi's core strengths lie in its development of in-house intellectual property (IP) tailored for efficient edge AI processing, enabling low-power, real-time applications in resource-constrained devices. This IP portfolio, which includes proprietary architectures for AI accelerators and sensor fusion, provides a technological edge by optimizing performance while minimizing energy consumption, as demonstrated in their A2000 AI video analytics chip.[6][71] Additionally, the company's India-based operations offer a significant cost advantage, leveraging lower development and manufacturing expenses compared to global competitors, which supports competitive pricing in emerging markets. Strategic initiatives at Netrasemi focus on expanding its product ecosystem through the introduction of advanced chiplet-based designs, which allow for modular and scalable SoCs to address diverse edge computing needs. The company is actively pursuing market entry into the automotive IoT sector, where its chips can support applications like advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS) and in-vehicle sensors. Furthermore, Netrasemi is digitalizing its design processes by adopting AI-driven tools for simulation and verification, accelerating time-to-market for new architectures.[71][72] In terms of capital allocation, Netrasemi prioritizes research and development, while maintaining a minimal focus on mergers and acquisitions to preserve operational agility. From the $12 million raised in its July 2024 Series A round, the company plans to invest in R&D and marketing, targeting the hiring of specialized talent and the prototyping of next-generation products like enhanced microcontrollers for smart sensors.[2]

### Growth Scenarios and SWOT

Netrasemi Private Limited's medium-term growth scenarios are shaped by its focus on expanding within the Indian semiconductor market, with projections of 150% revenue growth in FY25 and exponential growth from FY27 onwards through domestic expansion and scaling production of its AI SoCs.[24] This outlook is driven by increasing demand for edge computing solutions in IoT and surveillance applications, supported by government incentives like the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme, which could enable the company to capture a larger share of the burgeoning Indian edge AI market estimated to grow at a CAGR of 28.3% through 2030.[73] A SWOT analysis highlights Netrasemi's strategic positioning in the fabless semiconductor space. Strengths include a robust intellectual property (IP) moat, with proprietary chiplet-based architectures that enable efficient, low-power AI processing for edge devices, differentiating it from competitors reliant on generic silicon. Weaknesses stem from its dependency on external foundries for manufacturing, which exposes the company to supply chain disruptions and cost fluctuations in global semiconductor fabrication. Opportunities arise from India's PLI scheme for semiconductors, which provides subsidies and incentives for domestic design and production, potentially accelerating Netrasemi's market penetration and reducing import reliance. Threats encompass intense global competition from established players like Qualcomm and MediaTek, who dominate the edge AI chip market with superior scale and resources, alongside geopolitical risks affecting chip supply chains. In terms of M&A and alliance strategy, Netrasemi is poised to pursue foundry partnerships to mitigate manufacturing risks, with current use of international players such as TSMC for fabrication to enhance supply chain resilience. This approach aligns with broader industry trends toward strategic alliances in the fabless model, as evidenced by similar moves in the sector to secure long-term fabrication capacity.[74] Execution of these growth scenarios is closely tied to funding milestones, particularly leveraging the $12 million Series A round closed in July 2025 to invest in R&D and pilot productions, with subsequent rounds expected to fund scaling operations and international pilots by 2026.[5] This linkage ensures that revenue targets remain contingent on achieving key deliverables like the planned commercialization of the A2000 chip across more IoT verticals following fabrication.[49]

## Risks, ESG and Sustainability

### Operational and Financial Risks

Netrasemi, as a fabless semiconductor company, faces significant operational risks stemming from its heavy dependence on external foundries and imported components for chip production.[75] This reliance exposes the company to supply chain disruptions, such as those arising from geopolitical tensions, pandemics, or natural disasters affecting key manufacturing hubs like Taiwan.[76] Execution delays in critical processes like tape-outs, which Netrasemi has recently completed for its 12 nm AI chips, can further compound these vulnerabilities due to the complexity of coordinating with foundry partners.[77] On the financial front, Netrasemi encounters risks from high operational burn rates typical of early-stage semiconductor startups, which require substantial capital for R&D and prototyping without immediate revenue streams.[78] Additionally, its dependence on imported equipment, IP blocks, and raw materials creates exposure to foreign exchange fluctuations, potentially increasing costs amid currency volatility.[75] Liquidity challenges could arise if future funding rounds become scarce, as evidenced by the company's recent Series A dilution of over 40% equity to secure $12.5 million.[33] Market risks for Netrasemi include the cyclical nature of demand in AI hardware, where rapid technological shifts can lead to inventory gluts or sudden shifts in market priorities.[79] The company also contends with intense competition from Chinese firms, where billions in state-backed investments are fueling aggressive expansion in edge AI chips, as acknowledged by Netrasemi's founder.[26][21] Regulatory risks involve compliance with international export controls on semiconductors, which Netrasemi must navigate to ensure adherence to both domestic and global standards amid U.S.-led restrictions aimed at limiting advanced chip technologies.[75][80]

### ESG Practices and Mitigation

Netrasemi, operating as a fabless semiconductor company, outsources manufacturing to third-party foundries. This model aligns with sustainable practices in the industry, as it reduces the company's operational emissions while focusing on design innovations that promote energy efficiency. The company's System-on-Chips (SoCs) incorporate architectures optimized for power efficiency, enabling real-time AI applications in edge devices with minimal energy consumption, which supports broader environmental goals in IoT and AI deployment.[40]

## Investment View and Outlook

### Strengths, Concerns, and Catalysts

Netrasemi demonstrates strong intellectual property in edge AI chip design, having developed full-stack solutions using in-house IP for applications in surveillance, robotics, and drones, which positions it competitively in the growing edge computing market.[6] The company has secured substantial funding, including a Rs 10 crore pre-Series A round in December 2024 from Unicorn India Ventures, followed by a $12 million Series A round in July 2025 led by Zoho Corporation and Unicorn India Ventures, enabling accelerated R&D and production scaling.[81][5] However, as a young player in India's nascent semiconductor industry, Netrasemi faces concerns around execution risks, including long gestation periods for hardware development and challenges in scaling production amid global supply chain complexities.[82] These issues are compounded by the competitive landscape dominated by established global giants, requiring precise management of technical and market entry hurdles. Near-term catalysts include the anticipated commercialization of the A2000 AI video analytics chip, with India's first AI-ML chips from the company planned for release by early 2026, potentially driving early revenue and market validation.[2] Additionally, the recent funding rounds signal momentum for potential follow-on investments, supporting further tape-outs and fabrication of advanced SoCs like the A2000 and R1000. Key monitorables encompass R&D progress on 12nm node chips and securing initial customer wins in IoT and edge AI sectors to demonstrate product viability.[45] Red flags to watch include delays in tape-outs or fabrication timelines, which could hinder commercialization goals and investor confidence in this high-stakes industry.

### Case Outlines and Monitorables

Netrasemi's investment thesis can be framed through three primary scenarios: a bull case, base case, and bear case, each hinging on the company's ability to capitalize on the expanding edge AI market. In the bull case, Netrasemi achieves 10x growth driven by the broader AI boom, particularly in edge computing for IoT and real-time analytics, where its A2000 and R1000 chips gain rapid adoption among global manufacturers of smart devices; this scenario assumes successful scaling of production partnerships and further funding rounds to support international expansion, potentially valuing the company at over $500 million within five years based on comparable fabless semiconductor startups. The base case envisions steady 3x growth over the medium term, with consistent revenue from domestic IoT sensor deployments in India and gradual penetration into Southeast Asian markets, supported by the $12 million Series A funding secured in July 2025 from investors like Zoho Corporation and Unicorn India Ventures;[67] this moderate trajectory relies on reliable product iterations and government-backed semiconductor initiatives in Kerala, positioning Netrasemi as a niche player in low-power AI chips without disruptive breakthroughs. In contrast, the bear case projects stagnation amid intensifying competition from established players like Qualcomm and emerging Indian rivals, where Netrasemi struggles with supply chain delays for chip fabrication and fails to differentiate its SoC architectures, leading to limited market share and potential down rounds in future funding; this downside could cap growth at sub-1x multiples if geopolitical tensions disrupt global semiconductor trade. Key sensitivity drivers for these scenarios include the success of additional funding rounds beyond Series A and the rate of market adoption for Netrasemi's chiplet-based solutions in real-time AI applications, as higher adoption could accelerate revenue ramps while funding shortfalls might constrain R&D investments. To refine this investment outlook, next analytical steps should encompass financial modeling of potential revenue ramps based on projected AI edge device shipments, peer comparisons with other fabless firms like SiMa.ai or Edge Impulse in terms of valuation multiples, and on-site visits to Netrasemi's headquarters in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, to assess operational capabilities and talent pipeline. Catalysts such as strategic partnerships could further influence these models.

# Indian startups Netrasemi Mindgrove Technologies and Agnit Semiconductors plan chips

Technology Jun 01, 2026

Big news for India's tech scene: startups like Netrasemi, Mindgrove Technologies, and Agnit Semiconductors are gearing up to launch their own chips.

Netrasemi is already pilot testing its flagship chip with customers and expects commercial volumes by mid-2027.

Mindgrove is planning to drop new biometrics and industrial chips later this year, aiming for hundreds of thousands in shipments.

### Agnit readies gallium nitride defense chips

Agnit Semiconductors is preparing gallium nitride chips for defense use, with 5,000 to 10,000 units set for delivery in the next six to nine months.

Even though supply chain delays (thanks to a drop in imports from China) have made things tougher (a single tape-out can cost upwards of $3 million, with full production-grade quality demanding multiples of that), government programs like the India Semiconductor Mission are helping push innovation forward.

If all goes well, India's chip market could hit $180 billion by 2034.

Netrasemi's A2000 Chip Goes Production-Ready — India's 3 Chip Startups Race to 2027

Netrasemi's A2000 Chip Goes Production-Ready — India's 3 Chip Startups Race to 2027

SHARE

Kerala-based Netrasemi declared its AI chip production-ready in May 2026 with 3 OEM trials live. Mindgrove signed Bosch for field deployments. Agnit closed a $7.47M funding stack in March 2026 targeting 1 lakh GaN units. The prototype era is over; delivery pressure has begun.

Contents

Breaking developmentMass production entryUpdated funding — March 2026Verified data snapshotGovernment ecosystemRisk factorRoad to marketFAQ

| Metric | Value | Details |
| --- | --- | --- |
| India Semiconductor Market (2025) | $45 Billion | Expected to reach $100 Billion by 2030 |
| DLI Scheme Support | 24 Startups | Supported under the Design-Linked Incentive (DLI) scheme |
| VC Funding Attracted | ₹430 Crore | Raised by supported startups as of January 2026 |
| Sector VC Funding Growth | 10× Increase | From $5 Million in 2023 to $50+ Million in 2025 |
| Netrasemi Commercial Launch Target | Mid-2027 | Based on TSMC 12nm volume production roadmap |

Also Read: OpenAI’s $20B Chip Bet Is Shaking the AI Trade — Is Nvidia’s Dominance Finally at Risk?

---

## Breaking development

### Netrasemi: India’s first production-ready edge AI chip — trials live now

Kerala-based Netrasemi declared its A2000 AI system-on-chip production-ready in May 2026, with customer trials already underway, CEO Jyothis Indirabhai confirmed to The Economic Times. This is not a prototype announcement. The chip has cleared silicon bringup and is in active OEM evaluation.

Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala · Founded 2020 · Fabless SoC

- A2000 chip on TSMC 12nm node — integrates in-house NPU, VPU, ISP, and crypto engines
- Trials running with 3 OEMs in surveillance and automotive sectors as of May 2026
- Commercial launch target: mid-2027; volume production at TSMC Taiwan: 2027
- Second chip R1000 (AI/ML MCU for IoT) sent to TSMC fabrication in May 2026 via MeitY C2S programme
- Third chip A4000 (edge AI server chip, MeitY-backed) — fabrication-ready target: Q2 2027
- Total funding: ₹125 crore from Zoho Corp + Unicorn India Ventures (July 2025 Series A: ₹107 crore)
- One of first 4 startups to receive ₹15 crore DLI support from MeitY in 2023
- Plans to double headcount from 83 to 166 chip engineers within 12–18 months

The A2000 targets compact, power-efficient edge deployments, smart cameras, AI gateways, CCTV intelligence, and industrial robots. Engineering samples already run object-detection models under five watts. What sets this apart from earlier Indian chip announcements: there are actual customer co-development agreements in place, not just lab silicon.

---

## Mass production entry

### Mindgrove: Bosch signs for field deployment — 30% cheaper than imported alternatives

IIT Madras-incubated Mindgrove Technologies signed an MoU with Bosch Global Software Technologies in June 2025 to field-deploy its Secure IoT SoC across automotive, industrial, and consumer applications, the first Tier-1 global validation for an Indian-designed microcontroller chip. The company is now entering the final pre-commercial phase.

Chennai, Tamil Nadu · Founded 2021 · IIT Madras incubated

- Secure IoT SoC: RISC-V architecture, 28nm, 700 MHz — India’s first commercial-grade high-performance MCU
- Priced 30% lower than competing imported chips of equivalent class
- Bosch Global Software Technologies MoU (June 2025): field deployment and testing, SoC co-development, potential long-term supply agreement
- Pinetics commercial agreement (2025): two-year deal integrating Mindgrove chips into biometric, smart lock, and camera products
- Pilot deployments underway in biometrics, EV battery management, smart meters, industrial IoT, and wearables
- Total VC raised: ₹85 crore (including Peak XV Partners); DLI approval for Vision SoC also secured
- Vision SoC in development: targets CCTV, dashcams, ADAS systems, smart TVs

Unlike most chip announcements, Mindgrove’s Bosch MoU is not just a pilot; once assessments pass, Bosch will adopt the SoC for internal use and recommend it to its partner network across industrial automation and automotive. That’s a commercial pipeline, not goodwill.

---

## Updated funding — March 2026

### Agnit: $7.47M raised, 1 lakh GaN units targeted over 24 months — defence pilots live

Bengaluru’s Agnit Semiconductors closed a $2.6M seed extension in March 2026, led by Shastra VC, that fund’s first semiconductor investment. Combined with its 2024 seed round of $3.5M (3one4 Capital + Zephyr Peacock), total funding reaches $7.47M. The company is pivoting harder toward telecom infrastructure and power semiconductors, where GaN demand is structurally growing.

Bengaluru · Founded 2019 · IISc spinoff · Vertically integrated GaN

- India’s only vertically integrated GaN manufacturer, designs and fabricates GaN wafers, chips, and RF subsystems in-house
- March 2026 seed extension: $2.6M led by Shastra VC (Shastra’s first semiconductor bet); total raised: $7.47M
- Target: 100,000 GaN components in 24 months (revised from earlier 12-month target)
- 3 distinct RF products already in pilot deployment on Indian strategic defence platforms
- Pivoting focus to telecom infrastructure and high-efficiency power semiconductors (5G base stations, fast chargers, EV power)
- Global GaN semiconductor market: $6.7B in 2026 → $51.35B by 2035 at 25.45% CAGR
- China controls 87–90% of global gallium reserves, Agnit’s domestic GaN supply chain is a direct strategic hedge

---

## Verified data snapshot

### All 3 startups at a glance

| Company | Chip / Tech | Key milestone | Production target | Total funding | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Netrasemi | A2000 AI SoC, 12nm TSMC | 3 OEM trials live (May 2026) | Mid-2027 | ₹125 crore | Customer trials |
| Mindgrove | Secure IoT SoC, 28nm RISC-V | Bosch MoU + Pinetics deal signed | Commercial now (pilots) | ₹85 crore | Pre-commercial |
| Agnit | GaN RF chips + wafers | $2.6M extension closed Mar 2026 | 1L units / 24 months | $7.47M | Defence pilots |

---

## Government ecosystem

### The policy engine behind these companies

All three startups draw directly from India’s ₹76,000 crore (~$8.67B) Semicon India Programme, with the Design Linked Incentive (DLI) scheme as the primary instrument.

| Metric | Figure | Date |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Total Semicon India Programme outlay | ₹76,000 crore ($8.67B) | Launched Dec 2021 |
| DLI chip design projects approved | 23 projects | July 2025 |
| Startups with DLI/C2S EDA tool access | 72 companies, 278 academic institutes | July 2025 |
| Government committed under DLI | ₹234 crore across 22 startups | July 2025 |
| Total VC raised by DLI-backed startups | Over ₹380 crore | July 2025 |
| DLI startups total VC (updated) | ~₹430 crore | Jan 2026 |
| Sector VC funding 2023 | $5 million | Full year 2023 |
| Sector VC funding 2024 | $28 million | Full year 2024 |
| Sector VC funding 2025 | $50M+ (crossed $44M by July 2025) | 2025 |
| DLI long-term target | 100 chip cos; 20+ to cross ₹1,500 Cr revenue | 5-year horizon |

---

## Risk factor

### The supply chain problem: China controls the raw materials

India’s chip startups design domestically and fabricate mostly in Taiwan. That’s one vulnerability. The more acute one: China controls 87–90% of global gallium reserves, the key input for GaN semiconductors. In July 2023 China imposed gallium export licensing. By December 2024, it escalated to a full US export embargo. The US Geological Survey estimates a simultaneous full ban on gallium and germanium exports would cut US GDP by up to $9 billion.

- India currently imports 100% of its gallium and germanium, zero domestic processing capacity
- India’s National Critical Minerals Mission (approved by Union Cabinet, January 2025) directly targets gallium, germanium, and antimony stockpiling
- A separate National Critical Mineral Stockpile was announced in October 2025 as a direct counter to China’s export restrictions
- PLI scheme worth ₹7,280 crore for rare earth magnets launched to bolster upstream supply chain
- India has no domestic wafer fabrication facility; all three startups currently depend on TSMC Taiwan for production
- Agnit’s vertically integrated GaN model (IISc-backed domestic wafer fab) is the only current Indian hedge against gallium supply disruption

---

## Road to market

### Key milestones timeline

| Date | Event |
| --- | --- |
| May 2024 | Mindgrove launches India’s first commercial-grade RISC-V MCU SoC for secure IoT applications, built on 28nm technology. |
| June 2025 | Mindgrove signs an MoU with Bosch for SoC field deployment and joint chip development initiatives. |
| July 2025 | Netrasemi raises ₹107 crore in Series A funding led by Zoho and Unicorn India Ventures; 23 DLI chip-design projects receive approval from MeitY. |
| October 2025 | India announces a National Critical Mineral Stockpile following China’s export restrictions on gallium and germanium. |
| January 2026 | The Design-Linked Incentive (DLI) Scheme expands support to 24 startups, with cumulative VC funding attracted crossing ₹430 crore. |
| March 2026 | Agnit secures a $2.6 million seed extension round led by Shastra VC, taking total funding to $7.47 million, and targets production of 100,000 GaN units within 24 months. |
| May 2026 | Netrasemi announces its A2000 AI chip is production-ready; customer trials begin with three OEMs in surveillance and automotive applications. |
| Q2 2027 (Target) | Netrasemi’s A4000 edge AI server chip is expected to reach fabrication readiness. |
| Mid-2027 (Target) | Commercial launch of Netrasemi A2000, with volume production planned at TSMC, Taiwan. |

Read Next: Stocks in News, June 1: IndiGo’s ₹2,537 Cr Loss Shocks Street as Nifty Crashes 359 Points

---

## FAQ

### When will Netrasemi’s A2000 reach volume production and generate revenue?

Volume production at TSMC Taiwan is slated for 2027, with a commercial launch targeted for mid-2027. As of May 2026, the company is running paid co-development evaluations with 3 OEMs. Netrasemi has raised ₹125 crore total (July 2025 Series A: ₹107 crore from Zoho + Unicorn India Ventures) and is scaling headcount from 83 to 166 engineers. Pre-revenue stage currently.

### Is Mindgrove’s Secure IoT chip available to buy today?

Not at open retail. The chip is in the commercial pilot phase. Mindgrove signed a two-year agreement with Pinetics (2025) to integrate the SoC into biometric, smart lock, and camera products for OEM customers. The Bosch MoU (June 2025) moves it toward broader third-party adoption. Commercial shipments are expected within six months of completing the initial mass production order, per company statements.

### How many Indian chip design projects does the government actually fund, and by how much?

As of July 2025, MeitY has approved 23 chip design projects under the DLI Scheme, committing ₹234 crore of a combined ₹690 crore project cost. 72 companies and 278 academic institutions have EDA tool access. By January 2026, DLI-backed startups had collectively attracted ₹430 crore in private VC funding, nearly double the government’s own committed outlay.

---

All figures verified against MeitY, Economic Times, 3one4 Capital, Entrackr, PIB, and company statements. Last updated June 1, 2026.

# India's chip startups cross from prototype to production

iStock

Synopsis

## Indian semiconductor startups like Netrasemi, Mindgrove, and Agnit are nearing commercial production, with some already running customer pilots and aiming for large-scale output by late 2027. Government incentives are accelerating this progress, but worsening global supply chain pressures, particularly from China, are creating significant production challenges and extending delivery timelines.
